issues.claim: Summary: "chamber dues are quoted on request rather than published"
issues.problem: The chamber does publish a 2024 membership application PDF at mcrcc.org that appears to contain a dues table, but it is image-only: I re-fetched it and text extraction returned only the title, so no figure is machine-readable by our tools. The phrasing 'rather than published' is therefore slightly stronger than the evidence (published, but not readable). No dollar figure was asserted, so nothing numeric is wrong.
issues.fix: Reword to 'dues are published only inside an image-based 2024 application PDF that could not be read here, so actual figures are unverified; ask for a quote.'

issues.claim: PR Newswire NJ AI Hub release rated strength "Medium" (source_type vendor)
issues.problem: It is a promotional press release, which the rating rubric classes as marketing content (Low). Its 6,500 sq ft / founding-partner facts are confirmed, but the strength label is generous.
issues.fix: Downgrade to Low, or keep Medium only because the same facts are corroborated by the jerseytechandinnovation write-up (which repeats the founding partners).

issues.claim: NJ AI Hub accelerator terms (10-12 week cohorts, no equity, free space, MVP stage) rated Medium from a newsletter write-up
issues.problem: njaihub.org still returns HTTP 403 to this verifier, so the accelerator's own application page remains unread; the terms rest on one trade newsletter repeating Plug and Play's language. Rating is not overstated, but the single-source dependency should stay visible.
issues.fix: Keep Medium but retain the existing caveat that no primary program page was read.

claims_checked.claim: NJSBDC: nearly all services at no cost; all clients must complete an eRFC before any consulting; 100+ staff/consultants and seven regional centers

Rutgers-New Brunswick NJSBDC page is headed '(Serving Middlesex County)', says the Middlesex office is not offering in-person appointments, contact (609) 789-8364 / rutgersnb@njsbdc.com, Mon-Fri 8:30-4:30, Location 'TBD', Regional Director 'TBD'
Caveat: NJSBDC's Request for Counseling page lists The College of New Jersey as serving Middlesex, Hunterdon, Somerset and Mercer, conflicting with the Rutgers page

Business.NJ.gov: SCORE provides free, confidential, professional business counseling; Central Jersey Score covers Somerset, Hunterdon, Middlesex; Princeton Score covers Middlesex, Mercer, Burlington, Camden, Gloucester & Salem
Business.NJ.gov: NJBAC helps 'all at no cost and strictly confidential'; NJSBDC gives 'free, hands-on guidance'

NJ State Library databases free to NJ residents with a library card: Business Source Premier 2,300+ full-text journals / 1,100+ peer-reviewed; Regional Business News 75 business journals, newspapers and newswires; Reference Solutions 7 databases incl. U.S. Businesses and U.S. New Businesses

NJBAC publishes helpline 1-800-Jersey-7 (1-800-537-7397), 'Request a Meeting With Us', Business.NJ.gov live chat with NJBAC experts, downloadable NJ Small Business Manual, mentor/online-presence referrals
Division of Revenue schedule: LLC certificate of formation $100.00, LLC annual report $75.00, corporate/LP annual report $75.00, non-profit annual report $30.00
$75 annual report due every year on the last day of the month of formation; business responsible even without State notification; failure can result in revocation

Registration guide: all businesses should obtain an EIN (online <=15 min, EIN immediately; fax ~4 days; mail 2-4 weeks); all businesses must register for state taxes (NJ-REG) with DORES receiving an NJ Tax ID plus a Certificate of Authorization only if collecting sales tax; no state fee stated
Registered agent can be the business owner or someone else but must have a New Jersey address

Main Street Micro Business Loan banner: funding fully subscribed and NJEDA no longer accepting new applications (non-refundable fee cited); product was up to $50,000, 10-year term, 2% interest, no interest/payments year one, $100 application fee, $400 closing fee, formed at least six months, 10 or fewer FTEs, under $1.5M revenue

Small Business Fund: up to $500,000, in operation at least one full year, no more than $3 million total revenue, must provide fixed assets, home-based businesses ineligible, fees $300 application / guarantee up to 0.5% / closing 0.5% / commitment 0.5% all non-refundable

Small Business Improvement Grant: reimbursement up to 50% of costs up to $50,000, project minimum $5,000, must rent or own and operate from facility, home-based businesses not eligible for reimbursement, wage certification of greater of $15/hour or 120% of minimum wage, $100 approval fee, rolling applications until funding exhausted

NJ Accelerate: within six months of graduating an Approved Accelerator needs NJ tax clearance, at least 50% of workforce working or paying taxes in NJ, minimum 2 founders/C-suites at 100% professional time in NJ and 80% of time in New Jersey, targeted industry (incl. Information and High Technology); $500 Investment Benefit application fee

NJ Ignite: NJEDA grants plus workspace match cover tenant rent for three months, up to 14 months or $25,000; tenants need NJ registration, two-page executive summary, early-stage in qualified industry, fewer than ten employees, less than $1M trailing 12-month gross sales, at least one full-time NJ-based employee in the workspace, no prior NJ coworking lease, double-term commitment; workspaces match 1:2; no application fee stated

NJRIC is a free AI, cybersecurity and tech accelerator backed by the SBA; eligibility: registered and operating in NJ, AI/cybersecurity/IT or tech-related, two or more employees, revenues greater than $500k; includes coaching/mentoring, capital introductions and a Kean University Center for Cybersecurity resilience assessment

NJ AI Hub accelerator: Plug and Play runs cohorts (inaugural included) for 10-12 weeks each year; companies from MVP onward eligible; space free during the program, paid coworking afterward pending availability; no equity taken, no direct funding tied to participation

NJ AI Hub is a 6,500-square-foot space in West Windsor founded by Princeton University, the State of New Jersey, Microsoft and CoreWeave, and will house an entrepreneur's co-working space, workforce development and community events

TechUnited:NJ: 'Founders, entrepreneurs, students and individuals join free'; Builder tier includes member dinners and investor roundtables, weekly Ship & Run, monthly AI Demo Night, preferred pitching consideration at AI Demo Night, weekly newsletter; Innovator tier $3,000 under 50 staff, $6,000 to 250, $9,000 above

The CoWorking Space, North Brunswick rates: $35/day drop-in, 10 drop-ins $140, Weekday Co-Working $175/month, 24/7 non-dedicated $250/month, 24/7 private desk cubicle $350/month, virtual mail from $25/month, with free parking, printing and up to 10 conference-room hours monthly

UCEDC microloans: fixed rate between 5.0% and 7.75%, terms up to six years, as little as 10% down; businesses under two years old max $35,000; no prepayment penalties; eligible uses include equipment, fixtures, inventory, working capital, renovations to owned commercial real estate housing the business
Resource note: the NJ Ignite funding URL renders a general funding list showing '1-10 of 80 items', not the NJ Ignite program page

Middlesex County Regional Chamber of Commerce: 'more than 700 member businesses', programs, committees, newsletter/website advertising, event sponsorship, access to county officials; phone 732.745.8090
Data gap: the chamber's only public dues schedule is a 2024 application PDF that our tools cannot read
Caveat: njaihub.org and centraljersey.score.org return HTTP 403 to our fetcher
Recommendation arithmetic: $175 year-one state fees = $100.00 LLC formation + $75.00 annual report; $0 EIN and NJ-REG; owner can act as registered agent

Recommendation consistency: NJEDA timing rules measured from formation date (six-month rule for the micro loan, one-year rule for the Small Business Fund) support 'form early quietly builds eligibility' as a labelled inference
